related_questions.question: How bad does COVID have to be to be hospitalized?
related_questions.snippet: Most people with COVID-19 infections don't need to go to the hospital and will have a smooth recovery at home. Severe COVID symptoms that need medical attention include difficulty breathing, confusion or disorientation, and a bluish discoloration in the lips or hands.

related_questions.question: What to do if you test positive for COVID 2025?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19 in 2025, you should isolate, seek treatment, and take precautions. Specifically, isolate for at least five days, or until symptoms are gone and you have been fever-free for 24 hours, and wear a mask for 10 days. Contact your healthcare provider for guidance on treatment options, which may include antiviral medications.
snippet_highlighted_words: isolate, seek treatment, and take precautions

list.title: Isolate:
list.snippet: Stay home and away from others to prevent spreading the virus. You can end isolation after at least five days if you have no symptoms or if your symptoms are mild and improving, and you have been fever-free for 24 hours without using fever-reducing medication.

list.title: Seek Treatment:
list.snippet: If you have symptoms, especially if you are at higher risk for severe illness, consult with your healthcare provider or a local health center or department as soon as possible. Treatment, such as antiviral medications, may be most effective when started within the first few days of symptom onset.

list.title: Wear a Mask:
list.snippet: Continue wearing a mask for 10 days after your isolation period ends, even if you feel better, to further minimize the risk of transmission.

list.title: Inform Contacts:
list.snippet: Notify people you have been in close contact with recently that you have tested positive. They may want to take precautions or get tested themselves.

If you pass, the breathing tube will be removed so you can begin your road to recovery.
